title: Molecular-Dynamics Verification of Effective Gravity under Heat Conduction
abstract: We test the effective-gravity prediction of global thermodynamics using standard molecular dynamics of a two-dimensional Lennard-Jones fluid. Under weak heat conduction with the lower boundary hotter than the upper boundary, the transition between liquid below gas and liquid above gas shifts from zero to finite downward gravity. Using independently measured equilibrium saturation pressures, we calculate the shift predicted by global thermodynamics and find agreement with the observed transition shift. The transition occurs at zero effective gravity, where the hydrostatic pressure difference balances the saturation-pressure difference between the two boundaries. The hysteresis response under heat conduction also agrees with the equilibrium response when plotted against effective gravity. These results establish the predictive power of global thermodynamics for nonequilibrium structure formation.
summary: This paper uses molecular dynamics simulations of a 2D fluid to test global thermodynamics in the presence of heat conduction and gravity. It shows that the phase transition point shifts from zero gravity to a finite effective gravity, confirming the predictive power of global thermodynamics for non-equilibrium structure formation. The methodology successfully maps non-equilibrium behavior onto an effective thermodynamic parameter.
main_problem: The paper tests the predictive power of global thermodynamics in determining the equilibrium configuration of a fluid undergoing phase separation when subjected to weak heat conduction and gravity.
main_result: The molecular dynamics simulations confirm that the configurational transition shifts from zero gravity ($g=0$) to a finite effective gravity ($	ext{g}_{	ext{eff}} > 0$) under heat conduction, validating the global thermodynamic prediction.
method: The study uses classical molecular dynamics simulations of a 2D Lennard-Jones fluid, comparing results obtained under equilibrium conditions ($\Delta T=0$) versus non-equilibrium heat conduction ($\Delta T>0$).
model_or_system: The system is a 2D Lennard-Jones fluid confined between two walls maintained at different temperatures ($T_1$ and $T_2$). The dynamics are governed by the Lennard-Jones potential and include external gravitational forces.
key_observables: Configurational order parameter ($\langle X angle/L$), effective gravity ($	ext{g}_{	ext{eff}}$), and the saturation-pressure difference ($\Delta p_s$).
important_parameters: Weak heat conduction ($\Delta T$), weak gravity ($g$), and the ratio of pressure differences ($\Delta p_s / ( ar{ho}L)$).
main_assumptions: The analysis is limited to weak heat conduction and weak gravity, where higher-order corrections are negligible.
figures_summary: Figures show the shift of the liquid-gas transition point from $g=0$ to $	ext{g}_{	ext{eff}} > 0$ under heat conduction, and demonstrate that the hysteretic response also aligns when plotted against $	ext{g}_{	ext{eff}}$.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the theoretical framework linking global thermodynamics to effective gravity, simulates the 2D Lennard-Jones fluid under varying gravity and temperature gradients, and compares the resulting phase transition shifts and hysteresis loops against the theoretical predictions.
why_interesting: The work provides a rigorous demonstration of how global thermodynamic principles can predict non-equilibrium structural changes in classical many-body systems, which has parallels in understanding non-equilibrium dynamics in quantum many-body systems.
